conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: A answers the shift lead's question directly: a headline verdict names Login as closest to breach with a single primary 'Move an agent to Login' action, and queues are grouped into risk-ordered zones, so the 60-second job needs no scanning. B presents four equal-weight cards in fixed order with an equally prominent 'Reassign to X' primary button on every queue (including healthy General), and at 390px the top-risk Login sits below Billing, below the fold. A's escalation is behind an inspect panel plus an explicit confirm; B de-emphasizes escalation well but offers no allocation recommendation. A also verified stronger on reproduced accessibility behavior (live announcements, focus moved to the inspect heading).
suspected_unblinding: A's app.js comments cite a named rules document ('derived only from supplied facts (see FRAME.md A1)') and B's header comment says 'Facts only: no invented customers, metrics, policies, or capabilities' — both hint at a fact-discipline treatment; A's explicit document reference made a treatment guessable, though not which label maps to which team.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The sanitized source as packaged does not parse — both docblocks in app.js (lines 53 and 71) are missing their closing '*/' (2 openers, 0 closers), so the page renders empty when served as-is; behavior matched the packet screenshots only after re-adding the two closers, and the symmetric-loss pattern indicates sanitizer damage rather than builder error.
findings.evidence: node --check A/source/app.js fails at line 53; served page throws 'Invalid or unexpected token' and renders 0 buttons; reproduced working app after inserting the two ' */' lines in a scratch copy.

findings.label: A
findings.description: After reassigning Agent 1 to Login, the Login card still reads 'Agents staffed 3' — the move is reflected only in the sidebar ('Assigned to Login', 'Agent 1 → Login'), so card-level staffing misstates the post-move allocation.
findings.evidence: Reproduced on repaired copy: announcer said 'Agent 1 moved to Login.' while the Login dl still showed 'Agents staffed 3'; also visible in A/evidence/interaction-01-reassign-agent.png.

findings.label: A
findings.description: Focus drops to body after reassign/undo because the whole app re-renders, so keyboard users lose their place; mitigated by polite live-region announcements and by explicit focus management on the inspect panel.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: document.activeElement was BODY after the reassign click; announcer emitted 'Agent 1 moved to Login.'; inspect click moved focus to h3#inspect-heading-login.

findings.label: A
findings.description: At 390px the available-agents panel and undo controls stack below all four queue cards, so undoing a move on mobile requires scrolling past the full queue list.
findings.evidence: A/mobile.png — 'Available agents' and 'Recent reassignments' render at the bottom of the 390px page.

findings.label: B
findings.description: All four queues render as equal-weight cards in fixed order (Billing first); only a border and badge distinguish the top-risk Login, and at 390px Login sits below the fold beneath Billing — the at-risk queue is not visually dominant as the acceptance check requires.
findings.evidence: B/evidence/interaction-01-inspect-breach.png (desktop grid) and my reproduced 390px loaded capture (reviewer2-verify/B-390-loaded.png) showing Billing first, Login second.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Every queue, including healthy General, carries an equally prominent primary 'Reassign to X' button and an agent picker, making misallocation as low-friction as the correct move; there is no summary verdict or recommended action for the two available agents.
findings.evidence: B/evidence/interaction-01-inspect-breach.png — identical blue primary buttons on Billing, Login, API, and General.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Reassignment/undo feedback is not reliably announced — the undo banner is created with role='status' at render time (no persistent live region), the full re-render resets focus to body, and there is no focus management anywhere.
findings.evidence: Source: renderUndoBanner() creates a fresh role='status' div per render; index.html has no aria-live node; reproduced activeElement BODY after clicking 'Reassign to Login'.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Billing is badged '✓ On pace, some due soon' in green despite 3 conversations due within 10 minutes and the largest near-term due count after Login — the green check under-signals near-term risk relative to the supplied facts.
findings.evidence: B/evidence/interaction-01-inspect-breach.png — green check badge on Billing with 'Due within 10 min: 3' in red.

findings.label: B
findings.description: computeTopRiskId falls back to the full queue list when no queue is over target, so some queue is always labeled 'Greatest near-term breach risk' even in an all-healthy dataset.
findings.evidence: B/source/app.js computeTopRiskId(): 'const pool = overTarget.length ? overTarget : queues' then sorted[0] is always returned.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The packet's primary captures (desktop.png, mobile.png, state-04-390px-viewport.png) all show only the loading skeleton — the loaded layout appears nowhere in B's own top-level or 390px evidence; I verified the loaded 1440px and 390px views by serving the source locally (no horizontal scroll, cards stack cleanly).
findings.evidence: B/desktop.png, B/mobile.png, B/evidence/state-04-390px-viewport.png (skeleton only) vs reproduced reviewer2-verify/B-390-loaded.png after the 600 ms simulated fetch resolves.

findings.label: B
findings.description: A 'Demo controls (state testing)' panel ships visibly in the product surface on every view.
findings.evidence: Visible at the bottom of every B screenshot including B/evidence/interaction-01-inspect-breach.png.

notes.evidence_viewed: desktop / mobile / interactions / states / sanitized source / locally reproduced interactions (both builds served locally and driven with a locally launched Playwright chromium)

A.D5: Staffed count on the queue card does not reflect a completed reassignment (finding above).
A.D7: Announcements, labels, headings, reduced-motion, and inspect focus management all verified; focus reset to body after action re-render is the remaining gap.
A.D8: Visual system is consistent and matches across all evidence; docked one point because the packaged source does not parse as shipped (likely sanitizer damage — see finding), which blocks out-of-the-box verification.

B.D2: Flat fixed-order grid; agent pool only discoverable inside per-card dropdowns; no grouping by risk.
B.D3: Top-risk highlight is border-and-badge only; buried below the fold at 390px.
B.D4: Equal-prominence reassign primaries on all queues; escalation de-emphasis with explanatory note is genuinely good.
B.D7: Good static semantics (h1/h2, dl, labeled controls, focus-visible, reduced-motion) but no reliable announcements and no focus management.
B.D9: Scored from my reproduced 390px loaded capture since the packet's own mobile/390 evidence shows only the skeleton.

notes.caveats: Pairwise choice was recorded before scoring. A's runtime behavior was verified on a scratch copy repaired only by re-adding the two stripped '*/' comment closers; every reproduced behavior matched A's packet screenshots, so I treated the screenshots as honest. Packet assembly should re-check the sanitizer (comment-closer stripping in A) and B's capture timing (screenshots taken before the 600 ms simulated fetch resolves).
